detail.body:
## Summary vLLM has no launch configuration for the 2D unified-attention path on ROCm, so it falls back on defaults. On gfx1151 (Strix Halo) that leaves long prefill an order of magnitude below the hardware's bf16 peak. This series gives gfx1151 a 2D KV tile that matches the paged-cache block, a launch configuration for the 2D path, a wider query block for long prefill, and ranks `TRITON_ATTN` above `ROCM_ATTN` on gfx1151 so the tuned kernel is what gfx1151 actually runs. End to end on gfx1151 against `upstream/main`, TTFT improves in 20 of 21 model/prompt-length cells (−1.4% to −34.4%). The remaining cell, Gemma-2B-AWQ at 128 tokens, is flat (+0.2%). Decode throughput improves in 20 of 21 cells; the remaining cell, Qwen3-4B-AWQ at 128 tokens, is flat (−0.1%). ## Commits | commit | what it does | |---|---| | `[ROCm] Match the unified-attention KV tile to the block size on gfx1151` | A tile that straddles two KV blocks turns every tile load into a scatter, because the blocks are not contiguous in the paged cache. The 2D tile becomes the largest power of two that divides `block_size`, capped by the 64KB LDS budget. Matching them is worth 21% of TTFT on Qwen3-8B at an 8k prefill. Because the tile always divides the block, the last tile never reads a block-table entry past the end of the sequence, including for non-power-of-2 block sizes such as 1056. The 3D (split-KV decode) tile is not changed. | | `[ROCm] Give the unified-attention 2D path a gfx1151 launch config` | Sets `num_warps`, `waves_per_eu` and a per-phase pipeline depth for the 2D kernel, with the depth bounded by the same LDS budget. | | `[ROCm] Widen the unified-attention query block for long gfx1151 prefill` | Moves the query-block choice into `_select_query_block`; only gfx1151 is opted in. | | `[ROCm] Prefer TRITON_ATTN over ROCM_ATTN on gfx1151` | On gfx1151, `ROCM_ATTN`'s custom paged-attention kernel only covers head_size 128 / block_size 16 / GQA 3-16 / unquantized KV / no SWA, alibi or sinks. Everything else already falls back to an internal Triton path. | ## Scope Everything is gated on gfx1151 alone. gfx1151 is the only part benchmarked here, so the rest of the gfx11 family keeps upstream behaviour. - **Existing code touched:** only the 3 lines of `BLOCK_M`/`BLOCK_Q` selection in `unified_attention`, which move into `_select_query_block`. Everything else is additive. - `_get_tile_size` is unchanged, so the INT4 per-token-head and TurboQuant kernels that share or mirror it are untouched. - **Verification:** the kernel launch parameters `unified_attention` picks match `upstream/main` in all 2,800 bf16 shapes checked off gfx1151. The parameters compared are the grid, `BLOCK_M`, `BLOCK_Q`, `TILE_SIZE`, `num_warps`, `num_stages`, `waves_per_eu` and the `reduce_segments` launch. The shapes cover: - head sizes 64–256; - MHA/GQA/MQA; - block sizes 16–1056; - with and without a sliding window; - 2D and 3D decode, speculative decode, short and long prefill, and mixed batches. - **3D decode on gfx1151:** also identical to `upstream/main`. ## End-to-end results Setup: - gfx1151, concurrency 1, 128 output tokens, `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`. - No attention backend is forced: `upstream/main` routes to `ROCM_ATTN`, this branch to `TRITON_ATTN`. - Prompt lengths 128 / 2048 / 8000. - TTFT change: negative is better. Decode throughput (tok/s) change: positive is better. | model | head_dim | TTFT 128 | TTFT 2048 | TTFT 8000 | decode 128 | decode 2048 | decode 8000 | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Qwen3-4B-AWQ | 80 | −3.9% | −11.8% | −14.6% | −0.1% | +1.1% | +3.7% | | Qwen3-8B-AWQ | 128 | −1.8% | −7.0% | −9.6% | +0.2% | +0.4% | +1.5% | | Llama-3.2-1B | 64 | −7.0% | −3.2% | −6.4% | +1.3% | +9.9% | +30.2% | | Llama-2-7B-AWQ | 128 | −3.7% | −8.4% | −11.4% | +0.1% | +0.5% | +1.1% | | Gemma-2B-AWQ | 256, MQA | +0.2% | −8.5% | −26.1% | +1.4% | +14.9% | +50.9% | | Gemma-3-12B w4a16 | 256, SWA | −2.6% | −6.0% | −34.4% | +4.2% | +34.3% | +95.5% | | Qwen3.5-35B-A3B* | 256 | −1.4% | −3.6% | −15.0% | +3.9% | +23.7% | +56.8% | **The decode gains come from the fourth commit, not from the tuning.** At concurrency 1, decode runs on the 3D split-KV kernel, which this series leaves as in upstream. The decode column therefore measures `TRITON_ATTN` replacing `ROCM_ATTN`. ## Kernel microbenchmark This uses `benchmarks/attention_benchmarks` with `TRITON_ATTN` forced on both arms, which isolates the tuning from the backend switch. - **Arms:** this revision against its base, `upstream/main` at `764413559a`. - **Order:** the arms were run interleaved per configuration. - **Configurations:** all use `block_size` 16. Results: - **Prefill:** 21 shapes across 13 model configurations, all faster, 1.97x to 11.2x. - **Decode:** 12 shapes (`q1s8k`, one per configuration that has one) at 0.996x–1.008x, i.e. unchanged. | model config | shape | upstream | this branch | speedup | |---|---|---:|---:|---:| | `smollm2_1.7b` | `q8k` | 125.17 ms | 11.16 ms | **11.215x** | | `smollm2_1.7b` | `q8000s8k` | 125.58 ms | 11.47 ms | **10.946x** ‡ | | `llama_2_7b` | `q8k` | 253.56 ms | 35.00 ms | **7.245x** | | `gemma_2b_awq` | `q1856s8000` | 30.62 ms | 7.18 ms | **4.264x** | | `qwen2.5_7b_awq` | `q3968s4096` | 20.07 ms | 4.73 ms | **4.246x** | | `gemma_2b_awq` | `q2k` | 5.40 ms | 1.30 ms | **4.167x** | | `gemma_2b_awq` | `q2ks4k` | 15.08 ms | 3.71 ms | **4.060x** ‡ | | `qwen3_1.7b` | `q8k` | 51.31 ms | 12.67 ms | **4.049x** | | `qwen3_8b_w4a16` | `q3968s4096` | 22.46 ms | 5.58 ms | **4.028x** | | `qwen3_8b_awq` | `q3968s4096` | 22.43 ms | 5.59 ms | **4.013x** | | `gemma_2b_awq` | `q2ks6k` | 24.41 ms | 6.16 ms | **3.965x** | | `qwen3_1.7b` | `q3968s4k` | 9.80 ms | 2.72 ms | **3.601x** | | `qwen3_omni_30b_a3b` | `q8000s8k` | 181.37 ms | 50.97 ms | **3.559x** | | `qwen3_omni_30b_a3b` | `q8k` | 180.98 ms | 51.10 ms | **3.542x** | | `qwen2.5_1.5b_fp16` | `q4000s4128` | 7.25 ms | 2.07 ms | **3.504x** | | `qwen2.5_1.5b_awq` | `q4000s4128` | 7.23 ms | 2.08 ms | **3.487x** | | `qwen3.5_35b_a3b_w4a16` | `q413` | 0.59 ms | 0.19 ms | **3.117x** ‡ | | `qwen3.5_35b_a3b_w4a16` | `q413s541` | 0.83 ms | 0.27 ms | **3.079x** | | `qwen3_4b_awq` | `q4000s4128` | 14.08 ms | 4.93 ms | **2.860x** | | `qwen2.5_3b_awq` | `q3968s4096` | 7.20 ms | 2.54 ms | **2.840x** | | `llama_2_7b` | `q1920s2k` | 3.64 ms | 1.85 ms | **1.970x** | ‡ The harness reported a standard deviation above 3% of the mean in at least one arm. These are the least solid rows.
Model configurations (all block_size: 16, backends: [TRITON_ATTN], 20 repeats / 10 warmup unless noted) | config | q heads | kv heads | head_dim | batch specs | |---|---:|---:|---:|---| | `gemma_2b_awq` | 8 | 1 | 256 | `q2k`, `q2ks4k`, `q2ks6k`, `q1856s8000`, `q1s8k` | | `llama_2_7b` | 32 | 32 | 128 | `q1920s2k`, `q8k`, `q1s8k` | | `qwen2.5_1.5b_awq` | 12 | 2 | 128 | `q4000s4128`, `q1s8k` | | `qwen2.5_1.5b_fp16` | 12 | 2 | 128 | `q4000s4128`, `q1s8k` | | `qwen2.5_3b_awq` | 16 | 2 | 128 | `q3968s4096`, `q1s8k` | | `qwen2.5_7b_awq` | 28 | 4 | 128 | `q3968s4096`, `q1s8k` | | `qwen3_1.7b` | 16 | 4 | 128 | `q3968s4k`, `q8k`, `q1s8k` | | `qwen3_4b_awq` | 32 | 8 | 80 | `q4000s4128`, `q1s8k` | | `qwen3_8b_awq` | 32 | 8 | 128 | `q3968s4096`, `q1s8k` | | `qwen3_8b_w4a16` | 32 | 8 | 128 | `q3968s4096`, `q1s8k` | | `qwen3_omni_30b_a3b` | 16 | 2 | 256 | `q8000s8k`, `q8k`, `q1s8k` (10 repeats / 5 warmup) | | `qwen3.5_35b_a3b_w4a16` | 16 | 2 | 256 | `q413`, `q413s541` | | `smollm2_1.7b` | 32 | 32 | 64 | `q8000s8k`, `q8k`, `q1s8k` | Example (`qwen3_8b_awq.yaml`): ```yaml model: num_layers: 36 num_q_heads: 32 num_kv_heads: 8 head_dim: 128 block_size: 16 batch_specs: ["q3968s4096", "q1s8k"] backends: [TRITON_ATTN] device: "cuda:0" repeats: 20 warmup_iters: 10 profile_memory: false ```
## Non-power-of-2 block sizes Hybrid models, such as Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, pad the attention block size to a multiple of 16, for example 1056. Rounding such a block up to the next power of two would make the tile straddle blocks and read block-table entries past the end of the sequence. Using the largest power of two that divides the block avoids both. Measured on gfx1151 by calling `unified_attention` directly (`triton.testing.do_bench`, bf16), against the first revision of this PR: | shape | block | head_dim (q/kv heads) | first revision | this revision | |---|---:|---|---:|---:| | prefill 4096 | 1056 | 128 (32/8) | 19.70 ms | 12.22 ms | | prefill 512 | 1056 | 128 (32/8) | 1.71 ms | 0.56 ms | | prefill 4096 | 1056 | 256 (16/2), Qwen3.5-35B-A3B | 10.04 ms | 10.10 ms | | spec decode, 32 × q4 | 1056 | 256 (16/2), Qwen3.5-35B-A3B | 1.77 ms | 1.23 ms | | 3D decode, 1 × kv 2112 | 1056 | 256 (16/2), Qwen3.5-35B-A3B | 115 µs | 55 µs | | 3D decode, 4 × kv 3000 | 128 | 128 (32/8) | `OutOfResources` | 0.40 ms | | prefill 4096 | 48 | 256 (16/2) | 9.96 ms | 11.38 ms | | prefill 4 × 100 | 48 | 80 (32/8) | 0.96 ms | 1.17 ms | `block_size` 48 is the case where this costs time: the only power-of-two tile that divides it is 16. #56862, which masks the block-table load, would make a wider tile safe there. This PR does not depend on it. ## Accuracy Setup: - Full GSM8K test set: 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy (`temperature 0.0`, `seed 42`). - `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` in bf16, via `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` against a `vllm serve` instance on each arm. - Measured on `53b7271`. Qwen3-8B runs with `block_size` 16, whose attention launch parameters are identical in this revision. | arm | attention backend | accuracy | correct | invalid | |---|---|---:|---:|---:| | `upstream/main` | `ROCM_ATTN` | 0.8802 | 1161 / 1319 | 0.0% | | this branch | `TRITON_ATTN` | 0.8901 | 1174 / 1319 | 0.0% | No accuracy regression is visible. The +0.99 points should not be read as an improvement: - The two arms run different attention kernels (`ROCM_ATTN` vs tuned `TRITON_ATTN`), so their outputs are not expected to be bit-identical. - A net difference of 13 correct answers does not say how many individual answers changed. - The eval script records aggregates only, so no paired (McNemar) test was possible. ## Reproducing ```bash vllm serve "$MODEL" --trust-remote-code --max-model-len "$MAX_LEN" \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 vllm bench serve --model "$MODEL" --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len "$INPUT_LEN" --output-len 128 \ --num-prompts "$NUM_PROMPTS" --num-warmups 5 --max-concurrency 1 \ --temperature 0 --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,e2el ``` | `INPUT_LEN` | `NUM_PROMPTS` | `MAX_LEN` | |---:|---:|---:| | 128 | 32 | 4096 | | 2048 | 16 | 4096 | | 8000 | 8 | 8704 | | model | `MODEL` | |---|---| | Qwen3-4B-AWQ | `Qwen/Qwen3-4B-AWQ` | | Qwen3-8B-AWQ | `Qwen/Qwen3-8B-AWQ` | | Llama-3.2-1B | `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct` | | Llama-2-7B-AWQ | `TheBloke/Llama-2-7B-AWQ` | | Gemma-2B-AWQ | CONFIRM | | Gemma-3-12B w4a16 | CONFIRM | | Qwen3.5-35B-A3B | CONFIRM | The server log of every run records which attention backend was selected. Kernel microbenchmark, `TRITON_ATTN` forced on both arms, one run per configuration in the table above: ```bash cd benchmarks/attention_benchmarks python benchmark.py --config qwen3_8b_awq.yaml --output-csv upstream/qwen3_8b_awq.csv ``` GSM8K: ```bash vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B --port 8137 --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8137 \ --num-shots 5 --num-questions 1319 --temperature 0.0 --seed 42 ``` ## Testing On gfx1151, with the gfx1151 path enabled: ```text pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_unified_attention.py 1926 passed (upstream/main: 1879 passed) pytest tests/quantization/test_per_token_kv_cache.py \ -k test_triton_unified_attention_per_token_head_scale same result as upstream/main pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_attention_selector.py FILL IN pre-commit run --files clean (ruff, ruff-format, typos, mypy-3.10, SPDX, ...) pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files clean ``` ## Not a duplicate - `_select_query_block` is modelled on #52684, which tunes the same code path for **gfx1100** and is still open. The two are complementary and conflict only textually: whichever lands first, the other should rebase and add just its own branch to the shared helper. This series deliberately carries no gfx1100 tuning, since that part is not ours and is not measured here. - #56862 masks the block-table load in the same kernel. It is complementary: this series avoids the out-of-row read by construction and does not depend on it. ## AI assistance This change was prepared with AI assistance (Claude). Every line was reviewed by the submitter, and the measurements above were run and checked by hand.

+

+@pytest.mark.skipif(RocmPlatform is None, reason="requires ROCm")

+    """The KV-connector carve-out must survive the gfx1151 reordering."""
+    import vllm.platforms.rocm as rocm
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(rocm, "on_gfx1151", lambda: True)
+    order = rocm._get_backend_priorities(

+    )

 from vllm.utils.math_utils import next_power_of_2
 from vllm.utils.torch_utils import set_random_seed

@@ -937,3 +938,171 @@ def test_softcap_does_not_overflow_on_large_scores() -> None:
     ref = soft_cap * torch.tanh(scores / soft_cap)
     assert torch.isfinite(out).all(), out

+
+
+def _patch_arch(
+    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
+    gfx1151: bool = False,
+) -> None:
+    """Pretend to be a given AMD architecture, so these tests need no GPU."""
+    monkeypatch.setattr(triton_ua, "_ON_GFX1151", gfx1151)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("head_size", [128, 256, 512])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("block_size", [16, 32, 1056])
+def test_gfx1151_tile_size_fits_lds(head_size: int, block_size: int) -> None:
+    """One stage of K+V tiles must fit the 64KB gfx1151 LDS budget.
+
+    Regression guard for ``OutOfResources: shared memory``: a KV cache
+    ``block_size`` of 1056 rounds up to a 2048-deep tile, which overflows by
+    a wide margin at every head size.
+    """
+    tile = triton_ua._gfx1151_tile_size(
+        head_size, -1, element_size=2, block_size=block_size
+    )
+    assert tile & (tile - 1) == 0, "AMD Triton requires a power-of-2 TILE_SIZE"
+    assert 2 * tile * head_size * 2 <= triton_ua._GFX11_LDS_BUDGET
+
+
+def test_gfx1151_tile_size_preserves_gemma3() -> None:
+    """Gemma3's tile must survive the gfx1151 power-of-2 rewrite."""
+    for head_size in (128, 256):
+        tile = triton_ua._gfx1151_tile_size(
+            head_size, 1024, element_size=2, block_size=16
+        )
+        assert tile == 32
+
+
+def test_gfx1151_tile_size_matches_block_size() -> None:
+    """The tile must match the KV block, or every load straddles two blocks.
+
+    A deeper tile than ``block_size`` spans blocks that are not contiguous in
+    the paged cache; on Qwen3-8B at an 8k prefill that cost 21% of TTFT.
+    """
+    for head_size in (80, 128, 256):
+        tile = triton_ua._gfx1151_tile_size(
+            head_size, -1, element_size=2, block_size=16
+        )
+        assert tile == 16
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("head_size", [64, 128, 256])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("block_size", [48, 96, 1056])
+def test_gfx1151_tile_size_divides_block_size(head_size: int, block_size: int) -> None:
+    """A tile must not cross the last block of a non-power-of-2 block size.
+
+    Rounding ``block_size`` 96 up to a 128-deep tile makes a 95-token
+    sequence read a second block-table entry the sequence does not own.
+    """
+    tile = triton_ua._gfx1151_tile_size(
+        head_size, -1, element_size=2, block_size=block_size
+    )
+    assert block_size % tile == 0
+
+
+def test_gfx1151_tile_size_fp8_floor() -> None:
+    """An fp8 query keeps the 32-deep minimum tile even on a 16-token block."""
+    tile = triton_ua._gfx1151_tile_size(128, -1, element_size=1, block_size=16)
+    assert tile == 32
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("head_size", [80, 128, 256, 512])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("block_m", [16, 64, 128])
+def test_cap_num_stages_for_gfx11_lds(head_size: int, block_m: int) -> None:
+    """Pipeline depth must never push the estimated LDS past the budget."""
+    tile_size, element_size = 32, 2
+    capped = triton_ua._cap_num_stages_for_gfx11_lds(
+        3, block_m, tile_size, head_size, element_size
+    )
+    assert 1 <= capped <= 3
+    q_bytes = block_m * head_size * element_size
+    s_bytes = block_m * tile_size * 4
+    kv_bytes = capped * 2 * tile_size * head_size * element_size
+    # A single stage is the floor, so the tightest shapes still exceed the
+    # budget on paper; the tile shrink in _gfx1151_tile_size is what keeps them
+    # launchable.
+    assert capped == 1 or q_bytes + s_bytes + kv_bytes <= triton_ua._GFX11_LDS_BUDGET
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("max_seqlen_q", "nq_per_kv", "head_size", "expected"),
+    [
+        # gfx1151 long prefill: wide head takes 64, narrow head takes 128.
+        (256, 4, 128, (64, 16, True)),
+        (4096, 8, 80, (64, 8, True)),
+        (4096, 4, 64, (128, 32, True)),
+        # Below the long-prefill threshold, and decode, stay generic.
+        (255, 4, 128, (16, 4, False)),
+        (1, 4, 128, (16, 4, False)),
+        # Extreme GQA still respects num_queries_per_kv.
+        (4096, 32, 128, (64, 2, True)),
+    ],
+)
+def test_select_query_block_gfx1151(
+    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
+    max_seqlen_q: int,
+    nq_per_kv: int,
+    head_size: int,
+    expected: tuple[int, int, bool],
+) -> None:
+    _patch_arch(monkeypatch, gfx1151=True)
+    assert triton_ua._select_query_block(max_seqlen_q, nq_per_kv, head_size) == expected
+
+
+def test_select_query_block_untuned_arch_is_generic(
+    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
+) -> None:
+    """An architecture nobody tuned must keep the generic query block."""
+    _patch_arch(monkeypatch)
+    assert triton_ua._select_query_block(8192, 4, 128) == (16, 4, False)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("max_seqlen_q", "num_kv_heads", "head_size", "block_m", "tuned"),
+    [

+        (1, 8, 64, 16, False),

+        (4096, 8, 128, 16, False),
+        # Tuned gfx1151 prefill: wide head, then narrow head.
+        (4096, 8, 128, 64, True),
+        (4096, 8, 64, 128, True),
+        # Gemma-2B style MQA opts back out of the deep pipeline.
+        (4096, 1, 256, 64, True),

+def test_gfx1151_launch_config(
+    max_seqlen_q: int,
+    num_kv_heads: int,
+    head_size: int,
+    block_m: int,
+    tuned: bool,

+        max_seqlen_q,
+        num_kv_heads,
+        head_size,
+        element_size,
+        block_m,
+        tile_size,
+        tuned,
